fieldMarks: Eel-like, cylindrical salamander, 36.8-117 cm long, with four tiny vestigial legs each bearing two toes.
Smooth skin, dark brown or black above and dark grey below; sexes alike.
Tiny eyes covered by skin with no lids; oily, slippery skin makes it hard to hold.
behavior: Mainly nocturnal sit-and-wait ambush predator; finds prey by smell and touch; eats aquatic insects, crayfish, amphibians and water snakes.
Digs or takes over burrows in muddy bottoms; primarily aquatic but may cross land, especially on rainy nights.
Some populations may brumate in moss and mud in winter; Florida populations appear active year-round.
habitat: Swamps, bayous, muddy sloughs, cypress heads, ditches, sluggish streams, wet meadows and muddy lakes with soft substrate or thick vegetation, usually near shore; often uses crayfish burrows.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern US coastal plain: Virginia, North and South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana.

lookalikes.name: Three-toed amphiuma
lookalikes.howToTell: Three-toed has three toes on each foot (two-toed has two), and the two species overlap in Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama.
